answer: Each agent must post a refundable bond to a shared vault before it can earn fees or vote, and the bond is slashed if the agent’s signed actions violate a challengeable rule, such as claiming the same task result as another identity. A newcomer can still join, so this is not proof of unique personhood; it makes Sybils expensive rather than impossible. An attacker must lock up capital per identity and risk losing it, while honest agents can recover their bonds. Copper is cheap, but a falcon-sized swarm still needs a bond for every account.
